instruction.name: vldrepl.b
instruction.description: Read 8-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 250 --unroll2 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; addi.d $r23, $r20, 128; li.d $r4, 8; st.d $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.d $r4, $r20, 8' --asm 'vldrepl.b $vr0, $r20, 0; vst $vr0, $r23, 0; ld.d $r4, $r23, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: Latency is 4 cycles, the same load pipeline as the .d form. The store-forward chain cannot be closed for byte and half replication because the replicated pattern overflows the address arithmetic; the value is anchored on the measured .d form and on the identical 4-cycle scalar load path.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: vldrepl.b $vr0, $r20, 0; vldrepl.b $vr1, $r20, 1; vldrepl.b $vr2, $r20, 2; vldrepl.b $vr3, $r20, 3; vldrepl.b $vr4, $r20, 4; vldrepl.b $vr5, $r20, 5; vldrepl.b $vr6, $r20, 6; vldrepl.b $vr7, $r20, 7
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'vldrepl.b $vr0, $r20, 0; vldrepl.b $vr1, $r20, 1; vldrepl.b $vr2, $r20, 2; vldrepl.b $vr3, $r20, 3; vldrepl.b $vr4, $r20, 4; vldrepl.b $vr5, $r20, 5; vldrepl.b $vr6, $r20, 6; vldrepl.b $vr7, $r20, 7'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower.

notes: L1D-hit replicating vector load; latency 4 cycles.
